TOP: The top left adenosine monophosphate is adenosine-5' monophosphate. On the right is the adenosine, which is a pentose ring bonded right to an adenine. The structure of the ring, which is the same in all the molecules, begins with the apical O. O bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to adenine (boxed) and down to H. C bonds down and left to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH, left to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds up and left to C (5'), which bonds down to H and up to CH2, which bonds left to O, which bonds left to P, which double bonds down to O, left to O-, and up to O-. The 1', 2', 3', 4', and 5' carbons are labeled, from the carbon bonded to adenosine, down, and around to the carbon bonded to phosphate. To the right is adenosine-2' monophosphate. The structure of the ring, which is the same in all the molecules, begins with the apical O. O bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to adenine (boxed) and down to H. C bonds down and left to C, which bonds up to H (2') and down to O, which bonds down to P. P bonds left and right to O- and double bonded down to O. C bonds left to C, which bonds up to H and down to OH. C bonds up and left to C, which bonds down to H and up to CH2, which bonds left to OH.
BOTTOM: On the left is adenosine 3' monophosphate. The adenosine begins with the apical O. O bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to adenine (boxed) and down to H. C bonds down and left to C, which bonds up to H (2') and down to OH. C bonds left to C (3'), which bonds up to H and down to O, which bonds down to the phosphate group. C bonds up and left to C, which bonds down to H and up to CH2, which bonds left to OH. To the right is adenosine 2', 3'-cyclic monophosphate. This time, the apical O bonds down and left to C, which bonds up down to H and up to CH2, which bonds left to OH. C bonds down and right to C, which bonds up to H and down to O. O bonds down and right to P, which bonds up and right to O, double bonds down and left to O, and down and right to O-. The phosphate group is oriented in an "X" shape, not a "T" shape. C bonds right to C, which bonds up to H and down to an O in the phosphate group. C bonds up and right to C, which bonds down to H and up to adenine (boxed), then bonds up and left to the apical O.
